sample_unit: focus group participants (clinicians, developers, administrators, patient advocates)

links.outcome: Stakeholder perceptions of AI governance for validation, auditing, and use in the clinic
links.effect: Participants identified insufficient systematic governance on validation, auditing, and use of AI tools in the clinic across the Texas Medical Center.
links.quote: However, they also identified many challenges, including significant barriers to accessing quality datasets for training, insufficient systematic governance on the validation, auditing, and use of AI tools in the clinic, and limited patient involvement in AI development decisions.

links.outcome: Stakeholder views on accountability for AI-related patient care errors
links.effect: Accountability was unresolved; participants were split on whether the provider should take full responsibility for patient care errors resulting from AI.
links.quote: Accountability also remained an unresolved issue, with participants split on whether the provider should take full responsibility for any patient care errors resulting from AI.

links.outcome: Patient involvement in AI development decisions as reported by participants
links.effect: Participants identified limited patient involvement in AI development decisions as a challenge.
links.quote: However, they also identified many challenges, including significant barriers to accessing quality datasets for training, insufficient systematic governance on the validation, auditing, and use of AI tools in the clinic, and limited patient involvement in AI development decisions.

links.outcome: Where AI models are validated relative to where they are deployed
links.effect: Validation occurring primarily in well-resourced locations like the TMC raised worries about a digital divide, heightened for safety-net and underresourced settings.
links.quote: Discussion on validation of models occurring primarily in well-resourced locations like the TMC raised worries about a potential digital divide in health care.

unlisted_practices: Embedding bioethicists into AI development teams
Providing easy access to quality datasets for AI training

screen.reason: Qualitative focus group study exploring ethical and practical considerations, governance, validation, and notification practices regarding AI tools across a large medical center.
